cards.title: Proposal builder
cards.text: Write a 1-page proposal. Client: [NAME, BUSINESS]. Their problem in their words: [QUOTE]. What I'll deliver: [SCOPE]. Not included: [LIST]. Price and terms: [MY NUMBERS]. Timeline: [DATE]. Tone: plain, confident, no buzzwords. End with one clear next step.

slides.note: Every bracket is something only you know. That's the point.

messages.text: Rosa, Corner Crumb Bakery. Her words: "People call all day asking if we have gluten-free bread today." Deliver: 4-page site + a specials page she edits from her phone, map + hours. Not included: online shop, photos. Price: [YOUR PRICE], 50% upfront, 50% at launch. Live by Dec 1.

Rosa, you told me the phone rings all day with "do you have gluten-free today?" This site answers that before they call.
**What you get:** 4 pages + a specials page you update from your phone. Map and hours on every page.
Not included: online shop, photography.
Price: [YOUR PRICE], 50% to start, 50% at launch. Live by Dec 1.
Next step: reply "go" and I'll send the first invoice and a kickoff date.

caption:
How to write a client proposal with AI: vague prompt vs structured prompt

Round 1: "Write a proposal for a website for a bakery." It came back polite and generic: no client name, no real problem, a price of $[X] and an online shop nobody asked for.

Round 2, the structured prompt:

"Write a 1-page proposal. Client: [NAME, BUSINESS]. Their problem in their words: [QUOTE]. What I'll deliver: [SCOPE]. Not included: [LIST]. Price and terms: [MY NUMBERS]. Timeline: [DATE]. Tone: plain, confident, no buzzwords. End with one clear next step."

This one opened with the client's own words, listed what's in and what's out, and ended with a next step she can answer in one word.

The brackets are the whole trick: each one is something only you know. Fill them in and AI only has to do the writing.

Follow @nomorebusywork and comment PACK: I'll DM you 21 more prompts.
